_comment: Venue / local-ticketing sites whose event pages embed schema.org Event JSON-LD. Each entry: listing page(s) crawled for links matching link_pattern; every matched page's Event block imports. url_template turns a captured fragment (e.g. a Wix {"slug":...}) into the page URL. Category = mapsee frontend key. Optional "venue" {name, address, city, region, postal_code, lat, lon} FILLS a missing/partial event location for single-venue sites (every show is at the same place) - supply address+city+region and the sync geocodes it, or lat+lon to skip geocoding. Optional "skip_title" is a case-insensitive regex matched against the event NAME, for the non-events a venue posts to its own calendar (closure and private-hire notices). A "listing" need not be an HTML page: link_pattern is a regex over whatever the URL returns, so a site's own event sitemap is often the complete source where a calendar page renders only its first screenful.

sites.name: The Royal Room
sites._note: Live-music club, restaurant and lounge in Columbia City, Seattle. WordPress + WP Event Manager: /events/ renders only 12 cards and loads the rest over admin-ajax, so the listing here is the site's own event sitemap (declared in its robots.txt) - all 95 posts, no paging. Each event page carries a schema.org Event block whose startDate is NAIVE local time (no offset) and whose Location is the placeholder '-', so the venue block supplies the pin and, through it, the timezone the sync converts that naive time with.

_not_included.https://dmhsus.org/events/: Deconstructing the Mental Health System (Seattle 501c3). Refused from TWO independent networks, which is what settles it: this sandbox gets 202 with an sgcaptcha body on every path including /robots.txt, and a GitHub runner (172.208.127.83, an entirely different provider) gets a 403 on every path including /robots.txt. An earlier note here guessed the block was IP reputation against a datacenter address, because the challenge URL carries the caller's IP in its y= parameter; the two-network probe disproved that. The site is closed to automated clients, robots.txt cannot be read to establish permission, and we do not impersonate a browser to get round bot management - same line as sfbike.org. Re-probe with catalog_probe.py if that ever changes; the calendar itself is worth having. The route that does not depend on their WAF is to ask the org for an iCal feed.
_not_included.https://volcanictheatre.com/calendar: Volcanic Theatre Pub, Bend OR. VERIFIES and does not INGEST: the listing carries 25 schema.org Event blocks and every one of them is future, but none has a `url`, so all 25 take the listing's page URL as source_id and EventStore's (source, source_id) guard keeps ONE. The real links are tixr.com, which answers 403 to the production UA, so following them is a refusal too. Measured 2026-09-20: `verify` said 25/25 sampled events future, a full ingest kept 1. Not a jsonld bug — 239 of the 240 sites carry a link_pattern that matches real event pages, and the one that does not (Nectar Lounge) works because its Event blocks each carry a url.
_not_included.https://www.bendumc.org/events.ics: First United Methodist Church, Bend OR — an ics feed, recorded here because this file's _not_included is the one curation reads. STANDING ROWS: 27 VEVENTs, all future, all with an EMPTY LOCATION, and exactly ONE distinct title — 'In-Person Worship Service' twenty-seven times. It is a weekly service schedule, not a calendar of events, and it is the same shape as the City Park feed whose 365 vevents were 365 copies of 'Public Historical Tour'. Measured 2026-09-20: verify said 27/27 future, and a full ingest placed all 27 on the church's surveyed point — correctly, which is what makes it worth writing down. Proving a feed is not the same as reading what is IN it.
